## What's new

Threadnote 5.0.0-beta.6 makes project-scoped graphs more dependable in large monorepos and makes their scope visible while you configure a project.

Threadnote 5 helps an agent begin work with current, cited code context instead of repeatedly rebuilding an entire repository it does not need. This beta strengthens that everyday workflow for repositories with many applications and libraries.

### Keep a project graph focused as the monorepo changes

When you give a project one or more application or library roots, Threadnote follows the dependencies that belong to that project and uses that selection for indexing, queries, and the fresh code evidence behind an agent's Context Brief. The same configured scope now follows a project into linked worktrees, so normal agent work keeps using the focused graph rather than falling back to the whole monorepo.

Workspace discovery is more capable with the layouts common in established repositories: commented JSON configuration, TypeScript path aliases, nested Node workspaces, and Bazel packages. Threadnote also keeps harmless workspace metadata problems from making an otherwise usable project scope look incomplete. The result is less irrelevant graph staleness and fewer unnecessary full rebuilds when another team changes an unrelated package.

Use the project editor or the graph-scope commands to choose the roots, preview the selected code, and then let the installed lifecycle use that project-aware evidence automatically. Keep the full-repository graph as the explicit fallback for work that truly crosses the configured boundary.

### See the graph scope before you build it

The Manager's Edit Project dialog now scrolls correctly on smaller windows and displays the progress and result of a graph-scope preview. You can see what Threadnote is evaluating instead of being left with a disabled Preview button, then review the included projects, files, and diagnostics before committing to an index build.
